question: A set of data is given, the mean of the set is 40 while the median is set as 70. Find the mode of the data.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use empirical relation: Mode = 3Median − 2Mean

= 3 × 70 − 2 × 40

= 210 − 80

= 130

**∴ Answer = 130**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Mean = 40, Median = 70

**Formula used:**

Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean

**Calculation:**

⇒ Mode = 3 × 70 − 2 × 40

⇒ = 210 − 80

⇒ = 130

**∴ The correct answer is 130.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Relation

Mode = 3Median − 2Mean (for moderately skewed data)

Mean

Average value of data set

Median

Middle value when data is arranged

Applicability

Formula works for unimodal distributions
